rationale:
Evidence: across iterations 0 and 1, the robot left the line on every development track (60 trials each). max_error sat at about 0.061 m on all tracks, just past the 0.06 m limit, and rms_error was about 0.03 m throughout. steering_oscillation was small (0.06 to 0.14). Progress rose only on the oval (0.115 to 0.176), and stayed near 0.04 on the s-bend and slalom. Both gain levels failed in the same way, so gain alone is not the main cause.

Critique: I accept most of it. (a) kd 0.8 is a real problem. A 0.5-unit signal step at a sensor edge gives about 0.5 x 100 x 0.8 = 40 turn units, so the derivative term is dominated by edge kicks. The evidence shows little oscillation for kd to damp, so I cut kd to 0.2, which is still a modest damper (about 10 turn units per edge step, with kd 0.1 in iteration 1 at about 5). (b) The integral is too weak at ki 0.3. A 0.1-unit steady bias gives only about 0.1 turn units in 3 s. I raised ki to 1.0. The integral is capped at +/-2, so the maximum contribution is 2 turn units, which is bounded and large enough to matter against a constant motor mismatch. (c) The speed of 1.3 cannot finish a 4 to 5 m course in 3 s. I reduced base_speed to 1.2 so the robot spends less time in each bend and can hold the line. I am prioritising staying on the line over completion, since no design has yet finished a run.

Rejected or deferred: I did not change mass (the 0.6 kg change had no calculated benefit). I reverted it to 0.8 kg to reduce the number of changes. I also kept wheel_track at 0.14, because changing it now would confound the gain comparison, and kp at 2.0, which is the only gain change I have not yet tested in isolation. The critique notes that the failure may be a start transient, since max_error is nearly identical across gains and tracks. I have not changed the start behaviour, but this revision tests it: if max_error stays at about 0.061 with the same timing of line loss, the cause is the start, not the gains, and the next revision should address initial alignment and line_loss handling.

Changes from draft: kd 0.8 to 0.2, ki 0.3 to 1.0, base_speed 1.3 to 1.2, mass 0.6 to 0.8. Sensor layout, weights, wheel_track and kp are unchanged.

Expected result (hypothesis, not observed): max_error below 0.05 m, line_loss_events at most 1, and progress above 0.2 on the oval, s-bend and slalom. Completion is not expected. Decision rule: if rms_error rises while steering_oscillation stays low, the bias is not being removed and ki should go higher. If steering_oscillation rises, lower kp to about 1.5 first.
